480	It became a byword, and a thorn in the eyes of every hater of Torah
481	in Israel and around the world.
482	But the Sephardic picture is still missing.
483	And the truth is that the fall of the Sephardim was infinitely greater than the fall of
484	the Ashkenazim upon entering Eretz Israel.
485	If the Shoah struck and cut down the Ashkenazi Torah world,
486	then the Zionists, the Erev Rav, the leftists, the Mapainiks, call
487	them whatever names you like, damaged the Sephardic Torah world. The problem:
488	in the first years in Eretz Israel there was not one Sephardi from the Eastern communities
489	or Yemen who desecrated Shabbat. There was no such thing. But
490	deliberate, purposeful actions were carried out by the immigrants
491	here, all kinds of Bolsheviks who came from Russia, haters of
492	religion, who wanted to set the tone and turn everyone who came here into a secular person like them.
493	Anyone who knew the community of Yemen, Djerba, Baghdad, even though the Alliance had already entered
494	a bit, still had no open Shabbat desecrator who came here to Eretz Israel.
495	They just arrived in the land, and actions were taken to uproot religion from them,
496	from the Sephardim.
497	This is simple and clear.
498	The Rav of Brisk once said: why did they establish a state?
499	To uproot religion from the people.
500	Let's see you cut off peyot in Yemen, if the Yemenite police didn't come after you.
501	Let's see you try to undermine Torah study in Baghdad, if the Iraqi
502	police didn't come after you. But once you brought everyone here to Eretz Israel and you set the tone, then
503	nobody tells you what to do and how to act. So what happened, gentlemen? They tried
504	to uproot Torah entirely from the Eastern communities and the Yemenites, by force
505	and with brutality, with threats that they would not get food if they fled. Over food
506	they starved them if they wanted to keep Torah and mitzvot. They made girls and boys dance
507	away from their parents in terrible immodesty. They take a chicken, close the door, knock the
508	chicken against the door and eat it. On Shabbat they go
509	to the orchards, pick fruit: "See, nothing happened to me, what do you want?"
510	Mass Shabbat desecration. They threatened them that they would not get work, and that a school would not
511	get budgets if Torah and mitzvot were taught there.
512	They deliberately interfered with their Torah studies.
513	And now you'll say, you are fed by all kinds of preachers, demagogues of every sort.
514	No, gentlemen. All I am telling you now is not even a pinch of what a governmental
515	commission of inquiry established, which determined everything I am saying now.
516	It was in 1950, January 1950, that a governmental commission of inquiry
517	was established, called the Frumkin Commission.
518	There was a judge, called Gad Frumkin, and he was authorized by the commission to go
519	and examine the complaints that the immigrants had about secular coercion.
520	About secular coercion.
521	A government commission.
522	Not that today you are investigating what happened 50 years ago or 70 years ago.
523	You are investigating, you are speaking of January 1950. When was the state established? In '48.
524	You are speaking here of two years after, two or three years after the state's founding.
525	That is, things were fresh.
526	They received dozens of testimonies that they were interfered with, that their peyot were cut,
527	they said as if "shorn."
528	They cut their peyot, forced them to desecrate Shabbat.
529	There was enormous pressure on Ben-Gurion and Zalman Shazar and their friends, who tried to sabotage
530	the commission and its results. It did not help them. The commission was
531	published as an official government report, after collecting dozens of testimonies, that all these claims were
532	true claims. There was here, beyond any doubt, a drive to turn everyone secular and uproot their
533	religion. All of it was in the circles of the Histadrut, under Nachum Levin, who, following
534	the report, was removed from his post.
535	There is a sentence in Latin. I brought this sentence from the report; I read the whole report
536	to prepare this lesson for you.
537	It is written there, there is a sentence in Latin that says: whoever holds the government
538	determines the religion of the people.
539	So now, since the leftists were the ones who came here
540	at the beginning, they determined the religion of the people and uprooted Torah from them,
541	and forced on them what Stalin did not force. They already completed the job.
542	Why?
543	They could not tolerate the religious, Jewish, Diaspora, traditional marks.
544	They don't want Jews, they want blind ones, they want...
545	a pioneering, renewing, modern, secular state.
546	They could not tolerate all the religious, traditional, Diaspora markers.
547	And to our great sorrow, even the Ashkenazi religious were alienated from the Sephardi religious.
548	And so the Mapai people felt that the weak link in the chain could be broken.
549	Who was weak?
550	The Sephardim.
551	And so whom did they go after?
552	The Sephardim and the Yemenites,
553	the Moroccans and the Djerbans. To cut them off, they moved some of the children to secular educational
554	institutions, to boarding schools, to secular kibbutzim. They told them: your father is old-fashioned, your mother is
555	old-fashioned, now the counselor will teach you. And so it was. They laughed and mocked anyone who kept
556	Torah. One of the greatest scandals in this country is the abduction of the Yemenite children.
557	I tell you, people: they put their child, took him, "Your child is sick," they told them, "he is
558	sick."
559	They took him. I am speaking of thousands of babies.
560	Thousands of babies and children, not hundreds.
561	Thousands of babies.
562	They told them: your child is sick, your son, we will take him to the hospital.
563	After two days the parents come to the hospital to visit the child, and they told them: he died.
564	What?
565	Where is the body?
566	We buried him.
567	Here, they lift some earth for them: "Here, he is buried here."
568	Do you know what they did here?
569	Do you know what failures there were in this country when it was founded?
570	And what did they do with the... They took them to all kinds of kibbutzim, made them totally secular, and the best part:
571	when their draft time came, suddenly they receive a draft notice at home.
572	And then the parents understood: wow, how did a draft notice come to the house?
573	Why does it not say in the offices that he died?
574	Apparently he did not die.
575	Do you know what went on here?
576	Come, I have no time to get into those links, but understand how purposeful the drive to uproot religion was.
577	There was a lot of naivety, what can I tell you?
578	They believed simply that the State of Israel is the beginning of the redemption; the great Torah leaders were asleep with
579	the KKL collection box.
580	Do you know what the KKL box is, the Jewish National Fund?
581	Asleep.
582	I still remember when we were small children, in school they would put this collection
583	box in front of us. Do you remember the box of the Jewish National Fund?
584	A dunam here and a dunam there, clod after clod, Miri Regev.
585	What do you want?
586	They believed.
587	Do you know, now, from whom they were buying clod after clod?
588	From the Turks, from the Ottomans who ruled here.
589	For years the KKL did not sell land to Muslims.
590	Because when I put in money, I put it in to redeem the people's land, meaning the people of Israel.
591	There was a petition to the High Court about this: a Muslim petitioned, saying why doesn't the KKL sell to us?
592	The High Court said he is right, and they began selling to them too.
593	Do you understand what happened?
594	And this is money that I put in the box to redeem the people's land, to buy it from the Turks, and in the end they sell it
595	to Muslims. So what did we accomplish with that?
596	What did the sages benefit with their enactment?
597	They arrived in Morocco, gentlemen, and told the people in Morocco: we will bring your children
598	first and after that the elders. There is no time to bring the elders. They came to the parents
599	and told them: which yeshiva do you want, shall we take your children?
